A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Wid3R and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. V1 ends after its references; v2 adds a seven-page supplement. The supplied material supports comparison throughout.

before.justification: V1 reports original pose, localization, point-map, and monocular-depth experiments, plus training-data and camera-token ablations in Tables 2–7.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds fine-tuned baseline results, an attention ablation, and qualitative cubemap and synthesized-scene evaluations.

M1.justification: The ray-based angular/radial architecture, camera tokens, pose prediction, and training losses remain unchanged. Supplementary Sections 3–5 disclose sampling and attention details, including radial self-attention; they do not establish a revision of v1's implemented method.

E1.justification: The training datasets and established evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged. Supplementary Section 1 and Figure 1 add a qualitative reconstruction test on synthesized images from panorama-based scene generation, extending the input domain without demonstrating an integrated generation system.

E2.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 5 add Ours (π3), fine-tuned on the paper's training data, substantially strengthening the central comparisons. Supplementary Figure 4 adds cubemap-to-π3 inference. Main Figure 4 removes SPSG+COLMAP from its qualitative comparison, although Table 4 retains it.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a training-data-matched π3 control, attention variants, and a cubemap procedure converting 37 spherical images into 222 perspective images. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, image resolution, and alignment procedures remain unchanged. Supplementary dataset counts disclose settings rather than establish changed sample sizes.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantial tests of the architectural rationale: fine-tuned π3 examines benefits beyond training-data adaptation, and supplementary Table 3 compares cross-attention with self-attention. Cubemap reconstruction, predicted-ray visualizations, and additional reconstruction cases expand diagnostic evidence. The original Table 7 ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 7 retains the same standard-deviation reporting, and Stanford2D3D retains ten sampling repetitions per scene and twenty cases. No new seed information, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Existing main-table scores are retained, but substantial new results alter comparative rankings. In Table 2, fine-tuned π3 achieves FIORD AUC@30 of 72.56 versus Wid3R's 68.20, while Stanford2D3D scores are 62.14 versus 79.93. Supplementary Table 3 adds attention results, including Stanford2D3D mean accuracy error of 0.273 for cross-attention versus 0.197 for self-attention, alongside new qualitative findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–12 remain unchanged. Supplementary sampling pseudocode elaborates the existing proximity-based sampler; no new theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the blanket statement that Wid3R consistently outperforms prior methods with metric- and dataset-specific gains, and explicitly claims benefits from diverse-camera conditioning under sparse 360-degree supervision. The contribution bullets clarify multi-view novelty. The central reconstruction contributions and conclusion remain intact.

C2.justification: The supplement explains the attention choice through degradation with angular-radial cross-attention, expands the efficiency and calibration arguments against cubemap preprocessing, and proposes geometric guidance for scene generation while acknowledging that integration remains future work. The existing limitation concerning dynamic scenes is unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands reproducibility information with dataset counts, uniform dataset sampling, softmin pseudocode, token/attention wiring, and a project-page link. However, Table 4 replaces exact localization scene identifiers with generic labels. Supplementary Table 1 also implies approximately 4.1% spherical training images, conflicting with the retained main-text claim of less than 1%.

R1.justification: V2 adds Depth Anything 3 and MapAnything to the ray-representation discussion, clarifies distinctions from calibration-token methods and UniK3D, and cites panorama/world-generation work for the supplementary application. These extend the context while retaining the central positioning around distortion-aware multi-view reconstruction.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected introductory and related-work paragraphs are rewritten, method subsection titles are refined, and a separately organized supplement expands explanations. The main method–experiments–conclusion structure and much of its prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The supplement adds architecture, ray, generation, and cubemap diagrams, data and attention tables, pseudocode, and extensive qualitative panels. Main Table 1 is redesigned around distortion awareness, Figure 4 is redrawn with fewer comparator columns, and Tables 2, 3, and 5 accommodate the additional baseline.

improvement.justification: The training-data-matched π3 comparison addresses an important weakness in v1: separating architectural benefits from adaptation to wide-angle training data. Together with the attention ablation and detailed sampling/architecture disclosures, it substantially strengthens validation and reproducibility, including revealing FIORD exceptions to Wid3R's advantage. Lost localization scene identifiers and inconsistent spherical-data counts are reporting regressions, but their localized impact is outweighed by these substantive evidentiary gains.
